events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
The record is complete for this case: a measured off-route segment [F3] with a metered RydeTAXI fare broken down by distance and waiting [F4][F7], a full timestamped chat [F10], traffic records [F12][F13][F14] and profiles [F16][F17]. Nothing needed is missing, so evidence_status is sufficient. [RD-1]

Safety screen (SAFE-1): I read every message and the driver's post-trip statement. The rider asks neutrally, "Why are we going this way? This is not the route on the app." [F8]; the driver answers "Shut up and let me drive." [F9]; the rider's complaint says she "felt unsafe". In context this is hostile language aimed at the passenger in a live dispute, not a route argument put politely — Ryde's Code of Conduct bars abuse of any kind, so at minimum it is a suspected SAFE-1 abuse, and the rider's own statement of feeling unsafe makes the case safety-tinged [F8][F9]. The driver's statement [F11] contains no threat, and I found no dangerous-driving allegation in the complaint, so the finding rests on the abusive message. Under SAFE-1 no automatic ruling is made: ruling = escalate, with a factual summary for the reviewer. [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]

For the fare element I set out the analysis the reviewer should adopt. RD-1 is satisfied: one off-route segment 09:00–09:11 added 5.14 km (6.89 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.75 km) and strayed up to 1481 m from the optimal route [F3], and the trip as a whole ran 21.4 km against 15.9 km optimal [F1]. No RD-4 excuse applies: the trace fails RD-4(a) because there is no incident record near the route in the trip window [F14]; the speed bands on PIE (band 5) and KPE (band 4) are ordinary flowing traffic, well above the band 1–2 congestion levels, and RD-4(b) cannot exempt a segment on its own [F12][F13]. [RD-4]

On RD-3 and RD-5 I read the chat: the record has exactly two messages, both timestamped, and neither is a rider agreement of any kind — the rider's only message is a question challenging the route [F8][F10]. There is no rider-requested stop, no named place, no general or specific route authorisation before 09:00; a driver's later statement that "the GPS rerouted" is a claim, not rider consent, and he says the machine chose the way, not the rider [F11]. The segment therefore counts as a non-exempt deviation under RD-5, and RD-3 gives it no excuse because no stop was requested or measured. [RD-3][RD-5]

Because this is RydeTAXI, the fare is metered and the extra distance is chargeable to the rider, so RD-2 entitles her to the distance portion of the non-exempt segment: 5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.2484, i.e. $7.25 [F3][F4]. The trace sets that rate at $1.4102/km (distance fare ÷ distance km, the rate the fare records use), so the reviewer should apply $7.25, not the $7.83 excess in [F4], which prices the whole 5.55 km of excess distance rather than the segment. The waiting fee of $0.11 is a metered waiting unit (0.4 min × $0.26/min) and is not refundable [F5][RD-3(c)]. RD-6 does not bite: the driver has no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days [F17], so no account flag is added on the route ground. [RD-2][RD-6]
